candidates.title: Tourism SME big-data resilience (East Java)
candidates.shift: A study links digital readiness and big-data-driven supply chain integration to business resilience among tourism SMEs in a peripheral, non-Western geography.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative and borderline — tourism, not retail, but suggests SME supply-chain digitalization as a resilience playbook that could generalize to small-format retail in emerging markets.
candidates.evidence: Conference proceeding studies East Java tourism SMEs using Big Data Analytics to strengthen supply chain resilience.
candidates.initial_analysis: Borderline inclusion illustrating peripheral-geography SME digitalization as a resilience narrative; weakly evidenced but flags a possible cross-sector pattern in small-format supply chain strategy.
candidates.author: Yessy Artanti, Andre Dwijanto Witjaksono, Sanaji et al.

candidates.title: Continuous IoT food-quality sensing
candidates.shift: Mobile IoT sensing systems for real-time food-quality analysis are emerging as a research area, pointing toward continuous in-store/in-transit perishables monitoring rather than periodic checks.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — could seed new sensor categories for grocery cold-chain and in-store perishables, eventually reshaping food-safety compliance and insurance requirements for stores.
candidates.evidence: Research Square preprint on mobile IoT for real-time food quality analysis.
candidates.initial_analysis: From periodic manual food-safety checks to continuous IoT sensing, driven by falling sensor costs; if adopted, could change compliance/insurance requirements for grocery cold chains and shelf monitoring.
candidates.author: Fachrul Kurniawan, Fadia Irsania Putri, kurniawan Mohammad Naufal Yusuf et al.

candidates.title: Rainwater harvesting as systems-level water security
candidates.shift: Rainwater harvesting is being reframed as a component of social-ecological water-security systems in an arid, peripheral geography, not just a household add-on.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — could presage water-security-linked building codes or incentives in water-stressed regions that eventually reach commercial/retail construction standards.
candidates.evidence: Research Square social-ecological systems analysis of rainwater harvesting for water security in Uzbekistan.
candidates.initial_analysis: From household water-saving practice to systems-level water-security infrastructure, driven by climate-stressed scarcity; could inform future water-harvesting mandates for commercial buildings in arid markets.
candidates.author: Ugonna Oboke, Ahmad Hamidov, Акмал Акрамханов et al.

candidates.title: AI agents for materials discovery
candidates.shift: A new startup uses AI agents to accelerate discovery of novel materials, aiming to shortcut traditional R&D cycles.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — if AI-discovered materials reach construction-grade approval, could compress timelines for new low-carbon building materials; currently mostly software, so speculative for built environment.
candidates.evidence: Hacker News launch post for Discovered Materials (YC), an AI-agent materials-discovery startup.
candidates.initial_analysis: From human-led to AI-accelerated materials R&D, driven by compute-driven discovery pipelines; if it reaches construction materials, could shorten the path for new composites/concretes to reach code approval.

candidates.title: Robots built to disassemble machines, not just build them
candidates.shift: A robot specifically designed to salvage parts from broken machines extends circular-economy logic into industrial/robotic supply chains.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — could seed a 'reverse manufacturing' equipment class for disassembling end-of-life store fixtures, refrigeration, and HVAC units at scale.
candidates.evidence: IEEE Spectrum profiles a robot built to salvage parts from broken machines amid rising volumes of robot-made goods.
candidates.initial_analysis: From robots-that-build to robots-that-unbuild, driven by growing volumes of robot-manufactured goods needing end-of-life handling; at scale could create disassembly-as-a-service real estate uses near stores/warehouses.
candidates.author: Kohava Mendelsohn

candidates.title: Public space doubling as grid-scale battery
candidates.shift: A prototype 'architectural battery' installed in Ontario public space stores urban energy, blurring the line between street furniture/plazas and utility infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — reframes plazas and possibly parking lots/facades as energy assets; touches the open 'compute?/utilities' hunt zone if extended to retail sites.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily reports a prototype architectural battery installed in Ontario public space for urban energy storage.
candidates.initial_analysis: From architecture-as-shelter to architecture-as-utility-asset, driven by grid strain and climate pressure; if scaled, store facades/parking canopies could become distributed energy-storage nodes with new ownership and insurance questions.
candidates.author: Antonia Piñeiro

candidates.title: Zoning absence for drone-delivery launch stations
candidates.shift: A major retailer is proposing dedicated drone-delivery station infrastructure (seven pads, 83lb drones with 5lb payloads) in an industrial zone, exposing the lack of a zoning category for drone-launch infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — suggests an absence: no established land-use class for drone-launch facilities, foreshadowing new industrial zoning, noise, and airspace permitting categories.
candidates.evidence: Planner on r/urbanplanning reports a major retailer proposing a 7-pad drone delivery station with 83lb drones carrying up to 5lb payloads in their jurisdiction's industrial zone.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shifts drone delivery from a software/logistics problem to a land-use problem; if generalized, industrial zoning codes will need new drone-launch categories, noise ordinances, and airspace permitting frameworks.

candidates.title: Office stacked atop existing warehouse structure
candidates.shift: A steel-framed office was built directly on top of an existing harbourside warehouse for an energy company, treating the warehouse as a buildable platform rather than a static single-use box.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative single instance — suggests warehouses could be reframed as vertical-expansion platforms, relevant to flexible reuse of retail distribution real estate.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen reports OYO Architects built a steel-framed operations-centre office above an existing warehouse in Ostend for energy firm Elia.
candidates.initial_analysis: From single-use warehouse boxes to multi-layer program stacking on existing industrial structures, driven by land scarcity and adaptive-reuse economics; if generalized, could add office/amenity layers atop distribution real estate.
candidates.author: Tom Ravenscroft

candidates.title: Highway overpass reframed as buildable park platform
candidates.shift: Updated park designs build public/event space directly atop an existing highway overpass to reconnect a downtown to its waterfront.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — could be an early standard for capping highway infrastructure into mixed-use/retail-adjacent public space, opening new adjacent land value.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen reports Heatherwick Studio's updated Belvedere park design built atop a Louisville highway overpass to 'restore buzz.'
candidates.initial_analysis: From highway-as-barrier to highway-as-buildable-platform, driven by urban-core revitalization pressure; if replicated, could open new mixed-use/retail-adjacent land above existing highway infrastructure nationally.
candidates.author: Ellen Eberhardt

candidates.title: Heat + construction-code erosion + gendered informal labor convergence
candidates.shift: Extreme heat, unregulated construction, loss of vernacular building practice, and precarious women's informal labor are converging into a new class of climate-health risk in peri-urban/coastal India.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — names a governance absence: no framework yet links heat-adaptive construction codes with informal/gendered labor protection; a peripheral geography setting the terms of this problem.
candidates.evidence: Zenodo report documents intersecting heat, construction-practice loss, and informal women's labor precarity in Puducherry, India.
candidates.initial_analysis: From siloed heat/labor/construction policy to integrated cross-sectoral heat-resilience governance, driven by rising extreme-heat exposure in dense peri-urban geographies; could force new heat-safety construction codes and informal-labor insurance products.
candidates.author: K Suresh Kumar, Chris Kurian, Jane E. Hirst et al.

candidates.title: Slum upgrading as unintended climate-resilience infrastructure
candidates.shift: A staggered infrastructure-rollout study in Rio de Janeiro shows formal slum-upgrading programs produce measurable heat-adaptation health benefits as a side effect.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing — informal-settlement infrastructure investment could be reclassified as climate-resilience infrastructure; periphery (Brazil) generating a standard that could travel elsewhere.
candidates.evidence: npj Urban Sustainability study uses staggered Rio de Janeiro slum-upgrading rollout (2006-2019) to show heat-health adaptation co-benefits.
candidates.initial_analysis: From slum-upgrading-as-poverty-policy to slum-upgrading-as-climate-infrastructure, driven by empirical adaptation data; if generalized, informal-settlement investment could be reclassified and financed as resilience infrastructure globally.
candidates.author: Diogo Oscar Borges Prosdocimi, Kelly Klima, Maria DeYoreo

candidates.title: Water utility cyber-fragility as a building-dependency risk
candidates.shift: Rising ease of hacking water infrastructure is pushing cities toward new operational-security requirements for utilities that all buildings, including stores, depend on.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — the named cybersecurity trend is well covered, but the under-articulated edge is that building owners now carry utility-cyber-outage risk they don't control.
candidates.evidence: Smart Cities Dive outlines five steps cities can take against water-system cyberattacks, citing increasing ease of hacking.
candidates.initial_analysis: Already-named cybersecurity trend; the built-environment edge is that store/building operators now depend on utility cyber-resilience outside their control, implying new contractual and insurance clauses for utility-outage risk.
candidates.author: Robyn Griggs Lawrence

candidates.title: Named cyberattack disables municipal public-safety ops
candidates.shift: A cyberattack shut down critical public safety operations in a California city, an escalation of municipal infrastructure fragility.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative — already-covered incident, included as a trigger event; the retail edge is degraded public-safety response reshaping store-security staffing and loss-prevention insurance in affected areas.
candidates.evidence: Smart Cities Dive reports a cyberattack shutting down critical public safety operations in a California city, prompting a state AI-related response.
candidates.initial_analysis: A single named incident illustrating broader municipal-infrastructure fragility; for retailers, degraded public-safety response could reshape store-security staffing and loss-prevention insurance calculus.
candidates.author: Ryan Kushner
